messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: control-plane error-rate spike detected. metric: controlplane.gateway.5xx_rate at 18:02 UTC > 4x baseline. services implicated: auth-proxy, org-lookup, config-service. paging oncall: alice. incident id #INC-2026-0311-78

alice: Paging in. seeing 5xxs across multiple routes, spike started ~17:58. customer-impact looks real from initial dashboards.

ben: I’m on it — looking at ingress/load-balancer and upstream 502/504s. can you post the top failing endpoints?

alice: top errors by route: `/v1/auth/validate` 502->upstream auth-proxy, `/v1/orgs/lookup` 504->org-lookup, several `config/*` 5xxs.

charlie: I’m seeing `504 read timeout` from config-service when called from controlplane router. heap and CPU look fine on the config nodes.

alice: customers reporting via support: ACME, BetaCo, and two others. evan will share details. severity P1 for now.

evan: Confirmed — multiple support tickets about 502s on API calls, customers seeing request timeouts on login and org fetch. attaching snippet from support logs: `2026-03-11T17:59:42Z ERROR request_id=abc123 service=api_gateway status=502 upstream="config-service:5000"`

ben: running quick health checks. `curl -sS http://config-service.internal/health` returns 200 but latency is 1.2s under load. Gateway timeout configured at 1s — that will cause 504/502s.

charlie: That explains it. config-service has occasional long tails; we recently pushed a config fetch that queries downstream billing service with a 2s timeout. could be cascading. looking at recent deploys: `deploy/config-service@2026-03-11T17:30`

alice: rollback candidate? if we can't mitigate quickly, consider reverting that deploy to stop the tail.

ben: I can flip a routing fallback while we investigate: add a short-circuit to return cached config on timeout. pushing `feature:config-cache-fallback = true` via config-store.

charlie: doing that now: `curl -X POST https://config-store/api/flags -d '{"key":"config_cache_fallback","value":true}'`

incident-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-0311-78 - PAGER: oncall alice -> acknowledged by alice at 18:03 UTC

dana: Ops note: autoscaler scaled config-service from 3 -> 6 replicas at 18:05 in response to increased CPU, but latency tail not eliminated.

ben: added fallback flag. verifying...

ben: quick check: `http 10.0.0.1/v1/config?org=foo` now returns 200 with cached-marker header `x-config-source:cache` and 95% reduction in 5xx in last 30s. monitoring graphs look better. :thumbsup:

alice: Good. Customer impact still present but reduced. evan, please update support with mitigation and ETA.

frank: Heads-up: billing-calls in config path are still slow. we should open a hot ticket with billing team to investigate their latency spike. cc @charlie

charlie: reaching out to billing team now — sending them trace ids.

evan: Messaging customers: "We’ve deployed an emergency fallback to serve cached configuration while we investigate increased error rates. You may see stale config for a short window. We’ll update within 30 minutes."

ben: running deeper diagnostics: pulling p95/p99 for config-service RPCs -> billing downstream. p99 for billing calls is 4.8s, p95 1.6s. definitely root cause.

charlie: temporary mitigation plan: 1) keep `config_cache_fallback=true`; 2) throttle config->billing calls with local circuit-breaker; 3) revert deploy if billing fixes not forthcoming.

alice: New action items assigned: ben -> stabilize gateway fallback and verify no regressions; charlie -> engage billing + tracing; dana -> confirm autoscaler policies; evan -> customer comms. if anyone else is taking work, say so.

ben: I’ve added a short-lived circuit-breaker rule on controlplane router: `max_concurrent_upstreams=40, timeout=1200ms, fail_open=true`

incident-bot: Pager update: paging second oncall (dana) at 18:12 UTC

dana: taking second-oncall. reviewing scaling and LB config.

charlie: billing team responded — they have a GC spike on one node and are rolling a fix. estimated 12-15 min to stabilize. links to their incident: https://internal/incidents/BILL-2026-77

ben: given that, keeping fallback and circuit-breaker in place. lowering priority to degraded with partial customer impact. continue to monitor.

alice: agreed. move to monitoring phase but keep channel open. update incident status to `mitigated` when stable for 15m.

evan: Updated customers with the new ETA and note we applied fallback to reduce errors; support will escalate any regression.

charlie: billing reported restored at 18:28 and p99 for billing calls dropped to 420ms. removing heavy mitigations over next 5m to observe.

ben: rolling back `max_concurrent_upstreams` change and removing forced `fail_open` at 18:33. graphs look normal.

alice: confirm with support: are customers still seeing errors?

evan: No new customer tickets in last 12 minutes. ACME confirmed intermittent earlier but now OK.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-2026-0311-78 status -> mitigated (monitored) at 18:40 UTC.

frank: Postmortem notes to capture: cascade due to billing latency introduced into config-service; recent deploy contained an unbounded billing call; autoscaler increased capacity but tail latency caused gateway timeouts; good catch with fallback flag. action items: add request-level timeouts on config->billing with sensible defaults, add automated fallback for heavy paths, run load test for config-service with billing latency injected.

alice: Thanks all. keep eyes on dashboards for the next hour then we’ll call the incident closed. :white_check_mark:

ben: I’ll open the follow-up ticket linking traces and deploy diff: TRACK-2026-512.

charlie: I’ll coordinate postmortem and assign owners for actions.

incident-bot: Incident channel archiving scheduled; please move follow-up tasks to TRACK-2026-512 and PM-queue."
